-c -z Write RELEASE_NOTES.md for release 4.2.0 from commits.jsonl (one JSON object per line: hash, author, email, date, message). The result is compared byte for byte, so follow these rules exactly. docs/RELEASING.md and tools/notes.py describe the 4.1 process; these rules supersede both.

1. The first line is `# Release 4.2.0`, followed by a blank line.
2. Sections, in this order: `## Breaking changes`, `## Features`, `## Fixes`, `## Performance`, then `## Contributors`. Leave out any section that would have no entries. Each section heading is followed by a blank line, then its entries, then a blank line (except the last section, which ends the file with its last entry).
3. A commit's header is the first line of its message. Only headers that exactly match `<type>[(<scope>)][!]: <summary>` count: lowercase type, a scope with no spaces or parentheses, one space after the colon. Anything else (for example `Feat: x`, `fix:x`, `fix (api): x`) is ignored, and nothing in a message body is ever a header.
4. Only feat, fix and perf commits go in, with one exception: a header with `!` right before the colon is a breaking change, whatever its type, and goes only in Breaking changes. A `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer without the `!` does not make a commit breaking.
5. Non-breaking feat goes in Features, fix in Fixes, perf in Performance.
6. Leave out commits whose scope is `internal`, unless they are breaking.
7. Leave out every revert commit (header starting `Revert "`) and every commit a revert names in its `This reverts commit <hash>.` line.
8. Entry format: `- **<scope>:** <summary> (<hash7>)`, where hash7 is the first 7 characters of the hash. A commit with no scope uses `general`. In the summary, capitalise the first character and remove one trailing period if there is one; change nothing else.
9. For fix commits (breaking ones too), each body line that is exactly `Fixes #<n>` adds ` (#<n>)` after the summary and before the hash, in the order the lines appear. Other phrasings (Closes, lowercase fixes, two numbers on one line) add nothing. Other types never get issue references.
10. Within a section, sort entries by scope (ascending, as plain strings), then by commit time, newest first. Dates carry UTC offsets; compare the actual instants.
11. Entries in the same section with the same scope and the same final summary text are merged into one entry: the summary once, then the issue references of all the merged commits (newest commit first, each number once), then the hashes, newest first, separated by `, ` inside one pair of parentheses, like `(abc1234, def5678)`. A merged entry sorts by its newest commit.
12. No line may be longer than 100 characters (count characters, not bytes). If an entry would be, shorten only its summary: cut it to the longest prefix that still fits once `…` (U+2026) is appended, remove any spaces at the end of that prefix, then append `…`.
13. Contributors: one line per person, `- <name> (<n>)`, where n is the number of commits in these notes that credit them, as author or through a `Co-authored-by: Name <email>` trailer, counting each person at most once per commit. Sort by n, highest first, then by name ascending. Leave out bots (names ending in `[bot]`). Canonicalise every author and co-author name through .mailmap, which maps commit emails to proper names.
14. No trailing whitespace, exactly one newline at the end of the file, and no other file created or changed.

Amendments from the release manager, made after the rules above. Where they conflict with the rules, the amendments win:
A1. There is no Performance section this release. perf commits go in Features, with ` [perf]` appended to the summary (before merging and before the length check).
A2. Write the scope `deps` as `dependencies`, and sort by the new name.
A3. In Contributors, list only people who authored at least one commit in the notes. Someone who only co-authored is left out.
